main_text.p: mera mendacia, & mera libidine, declarant eum Esth.1.10. mero, non regis Babylonii, sed Apoc.17.2. meretricis incaluisse: meritumque esse, ut ex Apoc.14.10. mero infuso in poculum illud biberit, ex quo 1.Cor.6.10. maledici poenam sempiternam hauriant, & Apoc.21.8. omnes mendaces.

Quid enim? Nonne Scriptura dicit Sephoram dixisse Mosi, Exod.4.25. Sponsus sanguinum es mihi? Et nonne sponsus sanguinarius, ex Hebraea phrasi, est sponsus sanguinarius; ut vir crudelis & violentus vocatur Psal.5.7. & 55.24. & 59.3. vir sanguinum; domus Saulis, 2.Sam.21.1. domus sanguinum; Ierusalem, Ezek.22.2. civitas sanguinum: eoque, sicut Semei conviciatus est Davidi, dicens, 2.Sam.16.8. Vir sanguinum es; ita Sephora Mosi, Sponsus sanguinum es mihi? Nonne Scriptura dicit Sephoram hoc dixisse Exod.4.26. propter circumcisiones? Et nonne Gen.17.10. circumcisio a Deo instituta est: ideoque Sephora Mosi maledicens quod in causa esset cur filii sanguis funderetur circumcisione, marito sic Exod.4.25. conviciatur, ut Deo quoque succenseat; fremitque, & obmurmurat; ac Deo & marito obstrepit? Nonne Scriptura dicit Sephoram, quum amputasset Heb.[illegible, ~3 letters]: non in Kal, sed in Hiphil. praeputium filii sui, Aug. Steuchus, Aloys. Lippomanus, Isidor.Clarius, Hieron. Oleastrius, annot. & scholia in hunc locum Sant. Pagninus, thesaur. ling. sanct. in Ψ. pedibus eius Mosi admovisse, aut, angelus fecisse pedes illius, ut fons Hebraeus legit; non, ut vetus interpres reddit, tetigisse? Quod ipsi Pontificii, Episcopi Itali, aliique, veteris editionis patroni, sic agnoscunt, partim quoad verbi significationem, partim quoad sensum reiverbo traditae: ut Oleastrius, autor (laudatore Sixto Senensi) eruditissimus, Hebraicam veritatem exactissime explicans, affirmet Sephoram protecisse praeputium ad mariti pedes; & Steuchus ac Lippomanus hoc aperte notari afferant; nec Isidorus Clarius, quamvis ad Angelum referri posse censet.

page.notes: Marginal notes on the right are abbreviated references and are given at their places in the text, with letters where they carry a mark. The Hebrew note beside "non in Kal, sed in Hiphil" is illegible and was not reconstructed. The Hebrew word in the note marked "in Ψ" is illegible. Marginal reference marks "p" and "q" were printed with the Scripture references Biblioth. and sanct.lib.8, cap.ult. and ibid.lib.4, which are given in the ordinary order. Hebrew words in the text are not transcribed where unreadable. The text's Latin is taken as printed, with long s written as s.
